title: Ansel and the Signal
premise: Jude Yarrow, a navigator aboard the hauler Ansel, discovers a name on a ghost manifest that matches a colony she secretly recorded dying in silence—proof that someone in the Concord fleet ordered the colony's distress calls suppressed. To keep the truth from igniting a war between the Concord and the breakaway Meridian fleets, Jude fabricates a signal that makes both sides believe the colony still lives, buying time to find who signed the suppression order. As her lie frays under inspection by a Concord investigator she grows to love, Jude must choose between exposing the order and preserving the fragile peace. In the end she broadcasts the colony's true final recording to both fleets at once, forcing a shared reckoning that costs her her career, her anonymity, and nearly her life—but spares the fleets and finally gives the dead colony a voice.
about_author: Orsen Villalobos is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one answered before turning to fiction. He writes from a converted signal station on the Atlantic coast, where he still keeps a log of every ship that passes.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Jude Yarrow, POV. Aboard the hauler Ansel, Jude performs a routine navigation shift while the ship's hold carries backup cores of colonists who may never wake. She privately replays her encrypted recordings of Meridian Colony's final transmissions. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as professionalism, establishing her loneliness and her secret.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Auditing cargo records, Jude finds her own name—misspelled—on the manifest of the Vesper, a ship logged as lost before launch, listed as carrying relief supplies to Meridian Colony. The Vesper never flew; the supplies never went. Emotional beat: the chill of realizing her invisibility has been breached.

chapters.title: Static Where a Voice Should Be
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. She traces the Vesper's falsified flight plan to a Concord relay station and finds the distress channel from Meridian Colony was rerouted into a dead loop. Someone suppressed the calls. Emotional beat: dawning horror that the colony's death was not neglect but decision.

chapters.title: The Investigator Who Listens
chapters.summary: Dara Okonkwo, POV. Concord investigator Dara Okonkwo boards the Ansel to audit navigation anomalies—including Jude's unauthorized recordings. Sharp, fair, and observant, she notices Jude flinch at Meridian's name. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension laced with unexpected mutual respect.

chapters.title: A Lie With a Heartbeat
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. To prevent Dara's audit from exposing the suppression—and triggering a Meridian fleet retaliation—Jude fabricates a live status signal from the colony, buying time. Emotional beat: the vertigo of becoming the thing she despises, a falsifier of records.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Frequency
chapters.summary: Dara, POV. Dara decodes enough of the loop to suspect the colony is dead but cannot prove it; her superiors order her to certify the Ansel and move on. She refuses quietly, staying aboard. Emotional beat: her duty to truth colliding with her duty to the fleet.

chapters.title: The Signature in the Code
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Jude finds the suppression order's authorization signature—Admiral Ceylan Voss, a Concord hero. She also finds the Vesper's passenger list included her own sister, who died at Meridian. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose, and the temptation of vengeance.

chapters.title: What the Backups Dream
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. A power fault forces Jude into the hold, where she sits among the sleeping cores and confesses her lie aloud. The ship's engineer, Tam, overhears and, instead of reporting her, offers to help maintain the false signal. Emotional beat: the relief and terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Audit of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dara, POV. Dara confronts Jude privately with the inconsistencies in the colony signal. Jude, cornered, shows her the rerouted distress logs. Dara must decide whether to arrest her or help her. Emotional beat: the fragile alliance formed between law and justice.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Quiet Harbor
chapters.summary: Admiral Ceylan Voss, POV. Voss reviews the Ansel's audit flag and orders the ship rerouted to her flagship, ostensibly for commendation. Flashbacks reveal she suppressed Meridian's calls to prevent a panic that would have collapsed the fleet's supply line. Emotional beat: corruption wearing the mask of necessity.

chapters.title: Running the Dark
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. The Ansel goes dark, slipping between relay stations to reach a Meridian listening post where Jude hopes to verify the Vesper's true fate. Tam keeps the fake colony signal alive under Dara's improvised cover story. Emotional beat: fugitive intimacy—the crew becoming conspirators.

chapters.title: The Listening Post
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. At the Meridian post, Jude recovers the Vesper's black box: the ship launched in secret, was recalled by Voss's order, and its colonist-relief cargo was offloaded and sold. Her sister died waiting for it. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into evidence.

chapters.title: Terms of Trust
chapters.summary: Dara, POV. Dara drafts a report that could end Voss but would also reveal Jude's forged signal, likely sparking Meridian reprisals before any trial. She and Jude argue over whether the truth can survive its own consequences. Emotional beat: love taking root in the space between duty and justice.

chapters.title: The Signal Frays
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Meridian's fleet, believing the colony lives, dispatches a supply convoy that will reach the dead world in nine days—and find nothing. The lie's clock starts ticking. Emotional beat: the fabricated heartbeat Jude created now demands a body.

chapters.title: Boarded by Heroes
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Voss's flagship intercepts the Ansel. Voss boards, gracious and terrifying, and offers Jude reinstatement, a clean record, and her sister's recovered effects—in exchange for the black box and silence. Emotional beat: the seductive arithmetic of complicity.

chapters.title: What Jude Says to the Dark
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Alone in the hold, Jude plays her sister's last message from the colony and finally lets herself grieve. She decides the dead deserve their recording played whole, unedited, to everyone. Emotional beat: the turning point from survival to witness.

chapters.title: The Longest Watch
chapters.summary: Dara, POV. Dara stalls Voss's tribunal with procedural challenges while Tam and Jude rig the Ansel's array for a fleet-wide broadcast. Dara knows she is ending her own career. Emotional beat: love expressed as sacrifice, duty redefined.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. The climax: Jude transmits Meridian Colony's complete final recording—the distress calls, the silence, and the Vesper's black box—simultaneously to both fleets. Voss orders the Ansel destroyed; Tam takes a hit saving the array; Dara refuses the order to fire on grounds of witness law. Emotional beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: The Reckoning at Meridian
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Both fleets' convoys arrive at the dead colony and stand together in its silence. Voss is placed under joint arrest by Concord and Meridian officers alike—the first shared act of the fragile truce her crime nearly destroyed. Emotional beat: justice arriving outside any single law.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. At the joint inquiry, Jude confesses her forged signal in full, accepting censure. Her honesty, weighed against Voss's suppression, reframes the lie as the only thing that prevented a war. Emotional beat: accountability as the price of being believed.

chapters.title: The Names We Keep
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. The colony's dead are entered into both fleets' rolls, and the sleeping backup cores in the Ansel's hold are formally registered for revival. Tam recovers; Dara chooses to stay with Jude rather than return to a fleet that demoted her. Emotional beat: mourning becoming memory, love becoming home.

chapters.title: Ansel, Underway
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. The Ansel departs with a new charter: a joint Concord-Meridian recovery mission to wake the sleepers. Jude takes the navigator's watch, Dara beside her, and for the first time records something live instead of something lost. Emotional beat: the signal answered at last, the future open.
